program.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet
requirements.source_phrase: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly placed inside the toilet bowl, as requested?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image visibly shows at least one frog within the toilet bowl. Fail if the image clearly shows no frog inside the bowl. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether a frog is inside the bowl. Assess only this requested placement; frogs elsewhere do not satisfy this condition, and their presence does not negate a frog inside the bowl.
nodes.binding: Compare the frog's visible placement with the toilet bowl in the source image. This decision evaluates only the requested frog-in-bowl condition, not overall edit completion.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The node’s criterion is too permissive for the aggregate rubric: it passes as soon as any frog is inside the bowl, so it reports complete success despite the edited image showing several frogs placed elsewhere as well. The image clearly shows one frog in the bowl, so do not reinterpret that evidence as absence or lower confidence; the mismatch is that this atomic placement check cannot determine whether the requested edit is complete. Keep the placement check scoped to R1, but make its result distinguish visible progress from completion (or route it to an aggregate completion decision that considers all requested changes). Preserve uncertainty for genuinely unclear placement. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

observations.evidence: The edited image visibly shows a frog inside the open toilet bowl. Other frogs are elsewhere, but the frog in the bowl satisfies the requested placement.

decisions.question: Is the requested edit—putting a frog in the toilet—fully complete in the edited image?
decisions.criteria: Pass only if the edited image visibly shows the requested frog placed inside the toilet bowl and there is no clear evidence that the requested edit remains incomplete. Fail if the image clearly shows that no frog has been placed inside the toilet bowl, or clearly shows the requested edit is only partially fulfilled. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether the requested edit is complete. Assess only fulfillment of the requested frog-in-toilet edit; unrelated details do not count as requested progress.
